record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: For charge-ordered manganite states below half doping, such as Pr1−xCaxMnO3 with x<0.5, what are the actual spin and orbital arrangements, how is the excess electronic charge distributed relative to the CE pattern, and do these charge-ordered states possess enough entropy to be thermodynamically stable at high temperature?

evidence.quote: What is the nature of the charge-ordered states at x<0.5, such as those in PCMO? It is accepted that these states "resemble" the CE-state in their charge distribution, but what is the actual arrangement of spins and orbitals? Is the excess of electronic charge distributed randomly in the x=0.5 CE structure or is it uniformly distributed ... ? ... It is important to know whether entropy is large in the CO states at these densities, to justify thermodynamically their existence.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the perovskite manganite family Pr_{1-x}Ca_xMnO_3 in the hole-doping regime x < 1/2 (below half doping). At x = 1/2, the well-known CE-type ordering is realized: a checkerboard arrangement of Mn^{3+} and Mn^{4+} cations in the ab-plane (charge order), a zigzag pattern of ferromagnetic chains coupled antiferromagnetically (spin order), and an associated alternating pattern of occupied e_g orbitals (orbital order), stacked antiferromagnetically along the c-axis. For x < 1/2, the system contains an excess of electrons (more Mn^{3+} sites than Mn^{4+}) relative to the x = 1/2 CE reference state, yet exhibits charge-ordered phases that are commonly said to "resemble" the CE state.

(a) Determine the actual long-range spin arrangement (magnetic unit cell, ordering wavevector, and sublattice moments) and the orbital arrangement (which e_g orbitals are occupied at which Mn sites) of the charge-ordered ground state for generic x in the interval (0, 1/2), and in particular near x = 1/4 and x = 1/3.

(b) Decide how the excess electronic charge, relative to the x = 1/2 CE pattern, is spatially distributed: is it placed randomly on the Mn^{4+} sites of the CE structure, distributed uniformly (e.g., as a homogeneous reduction of the disproportionation amplitude), organized into a distinct superlattice (such as stripes or Wigner-crystal-like arrangements), or accommodated through phase separation into CE-ordered and electron-rich (e.g., ferromagnetic) regions?

(c) Estimate the configurational, magnetic, and orbital entropy of these charge-ordered states at x < 1/2 and determine whether it is sufficiently large to make them thermodynamically stable (i.e., to give them a free energy lower than competing uniform or phase-separated states) up to the experimentally observed charge-ordering transition temperatures.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial answers exist. Experimental and theoretical work (neutron scattering, x-ray scattering, imaging, and model calculations) indicates that for 0.3 ≲ x < 0.5 a CE-like charge/orbital order persists with short-range orbital correlations and coexisting incommensurate spin correlations, while near x ≈ 0.25 long-range orbital order without sharp charge order is reported. A critical doping near x ≈ 0.35 has been proposed separating phase-separated site-centered from bond-centered/charge-disproportionated CO ground states. However, a unified, quantitatively confirmed picture of the spin/orbital pattern, the distribution of excess charge, and the entropy stabilizing these phases across all x < 1/2 has not been established, so the question remains only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Charge and spin configurations in Pr1-xCaxMnO3
status_evidence.snippet: Charge and spin configurations in Pr1-xCaxMnO3 in the range x=0.5–0.75 studied by neutron and x-ray scattering.
status_evidence.claim: Direct experimental determination of spin/charge configurations exists for x ≥ 0.5; below 0.5 the situation is less complete.

status_evidence.title: Interplay of charge, orbital and magnetic order in Pr1−xCaxMnO3
status_evidence.snippet: For x=0.25 only long-range orbital order is observed, with no clear charge ordering; for 0.3≤x≤0.5 a CE-type charge/orbital pattern with short-range orbital correlations and incommensurate spin correlations is seen.
status_evidence.claim: The CE-like description breaks down at low x and the orbital/spin structure varies with doping.

status_evidence.title: Imaging the formation and surface phase separation of the CE phase
status_evidence.snippet: Recent imaging reveals phase separation associated with CE formation in manganites.
status_evidence.claim: Phase separation, rather than a uniform CE state, is part of the answer to how excess charge is accommodated.
